description:
FILED + DONE s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-16) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/tie_fetch_count.t.

THE RULE: perl calls a tied scalar's FETCH exactly ONCE per operator.  The
count is observable -- a FETCH may count, log, or advance an iterator -- so a
second read is a silent wrong with the program's own side effects in it.

WHAT WAS WRONG: an operator that first INSPECTS its operand (to choose a
string arm over a numeric one, or to find the old value of a postfix ++) and
then COERCES the same PLACE with to-string / to-number reads it TWICE.  Nine
operators did:

  probes/fetch1.pl + fetch2.pl + fetch3.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 2ac855aa
    operator     perl   PCL(before)   PCL(after)
    unary -        1        2            1
    x (scalar)     1        2            1
    post ++        1        2            1
    post --        1        2            1
    &              1        2            1
    ^              1        2            1
    |              1        2            1
    ~              1        2            1
    length         1        2            1

THE FIX: one helper `%p-read-operand (place val)` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp --
the coercion takes the value the inspection already produced.  Sites:
%p-neg, %p-str-x-plain, %p-binary-bit-op (new, shared by p-bit-and/or/xor),
p-bit-not, p-post++'s and p-post--'s default arms, p-length.
%p-bitwise-operand-kind returns the read value as a SECOND value;
p-string-bitwise-operand-p is deleted (it took the operand and so read it
again).

THE NARROWING IS LOAD-BEARING, and the first spelling got it wrong: a bare
`unbox` before the coercion broke `~ [1] == ~ [1]`, which must answer "diff"
(perl numifies a reference to the referent's ADDRESS, and PCL derives that
address from the BOX).  So `%p-read-operand` hands back the PLACE when the box
carries a bless class (the `""` / `0+` / `++` handlers), the is-ref flag, or a
cached numeric half (a dualvar like $! numifies to the errno, not by
re-reading its string) -- that is `%p-storable-raw`'s rule without its gate.

GUARD: Pl/t/tie-fetch-once-01.t, 15 rows -- 9 FETCH counts and 6 rows that ARE
the exception (overloaded neg/x/length/&, a dualvar through &, two distinct
refs through ~).  Inverse-verified on a `git archive 2ac855aa` extraction: the
9 fail reading 2, the 6 pass.  ir-spec 2.2b rule 5 is normative.

NOT FIXED HERE, filed as #1814: the ZERO-FETCH half of the same family --
`@a = ($tied)` does not FETCH at all (it stores the tie proxy into the
element), which is a different mechanism (the aggregate COPY path) and a worse
bug.  That is t/op/tie_fetch_count.t row 14, and `<$tied_glob>` (row 58) is a
third, also 0.

AFTERMATH (s473t6a resume, 2026-09-17): the companion op/ leg shows this fix is
14 rows FIXED and 9 rows BROKEN in t/op/bop.t (net 469/28 -> 474/23).  The 9
assert fetches($x)==2 after a COMPOUND |= &= ^= and were passing only because
the old DOUBLE read made that count 2 by accident -- the same accident made the
VOID count 2, which perl says is 1.  The residue is task #1840 (a compound
assignment returns its LEFT OPERAND AS AN LVALUE; the gap predates this fix --
`+=` and `.=` answered 1 on main too).  op/tie.t also gained a row (DATA record
44, "Bug 68192 - numeric ops not calling mg_get when tied scalar holds a ref").
subject: An operator must read its operand ONCE: nine operators called a tied scalar's FETCH twice (unary -, x, post ++/--, & ^ | ~, length)
